  <div class="dc-reveal" style="padding-top:5rem;">
    <p class="dc-body" style="font-size:1.05rem;margin-bottom:1.5rem;">
      I am an Assistant Professor in Urban Data for Design at TU Delft. I work at the intersection of urbanism, landscape architecture, and spatial data science — with urban resilience and climate adaptation as the central thread.
    </p>
    <p class="dc-body" style="margin-bottom:1.5rem;">
      My starting point is a conviction: <strong>the digital revolution is not a technical revolution — it is a mental one.</strong> We gave ourselves augmented tools not to do the same things faster, but to think at a different level of complexity. A complexity that entangles spatial scales from the yard to the planet, and temporal scales from a human lifetime to geological cycles — all in the light of the acceleration that digitalization has brought about.
    </p>
    <div class="dc-pull">
      <p>Data are not neutral. They are political — generated by political will, reflecting it, and dictating it.</p>
    </div>
    <p class="dc-body" style="margin-bottom:1.5rem;">
      Digital tools let us focus on <strong>flows</strong>, on spatial interactions decoupled from the concept of proximity, to unpack challenges that were previously too complex to hold: climate change, environmental degradation, and the persistent failure of cities to keep pace with the urgency of adaptation.
    </p>
    <p class="dc-body">
      I also work extensively with AI — exploring what it means for how we teach and practice spatial design, and how computational intelligence might become a genuine design partner rather than a shortcut.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- New Cities -->
<div style="padding:5rem 4rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-md);">
  <div class="dc-reveal" style="max-width:820px;margin:0 auto;text-align:center;">
    <div class="dc-eyebrow" style="justify-content:center;">What I mean by new cities</div>
    <h2 class="dc-heading" style="font-size:clamp(2rem,3.5vw,3rem);margin-bottom:1.5rem;">
      Just. Livable.<br>Climate-proof. <em class="dc-heading-em">Alive.</em>
    </h2>
    <p class="dc-body" style="max-width:640px;margin:0 auto 2rem;text-align:left;">
      Designing for climate adaptation carries an imperative: <strong>bring nature back into cities</strong>. Whether adapting to heat, managing floods, increasing biodiversity, or enabling phytoremediation — the answer points toward landscape. Projects — realized or stuck in a drawer — tell us what we believe, and how we translate those beliefs into spatial form.
    </p>
    <p class="dc-body" style="max-width:640px;margin:0 auto;text-align:left;">
      This is how spatial planners contribute to the re-territorialization of cities (Raffestin): linking them to their surrounding environment, framing them in a global network where <strong>relational position has overtaken geographical location</strong>. Data-driven approaches can speed up adaptation, lower the costs of analysis, and democratize planning in areas that lack the economic and governance resources to act alone.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Questions -->
<div style="padding:5rem 4rem;background:var(--lime-pale);border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-md);">

        <p style="font-family:var(--f-display);font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.7;">Data reflect political choices about what gets measured, who gets counted, and what is made visible. Reading data critically is reading power.</p>
      </div>
      <div style="background:var(--paper);padding:2rem 2.25rem;">
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-serif);font-style:italic;font-size:1.05rem;color:var(--forest);line-height:1.5;margin-bottom:0.75rem;">"How can we design smarter, faster, more systemic adaptation?"</p>
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-display);font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.7;">Automated digital workflows allow replicability and scaling. What takes months of analysis can be reduced to hours — and applied across geographies that lack the resources to act alone.</p>
      </div>
      <div style="background:var(--paper);padding:2rem 2.25rem;">
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-serif);font-style:italic;font-size:1.05rem;color:var(--forest);line-height:1.5;margin-bottom:0.75rem;">"How can data-driven approaches unlock design creativity?"</p>
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-display);font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.7;">Maps are instruments of discovery. Data allow the creation of infinite maps that reveal spatial patterns, unexpected relationships, and new design hypotheses.</p>
      </div>
      <div style="background:var(--paper);padding:2rem 2.25rem;">
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-serif);font-style:italic;font-size:1.05rem;color:var(--forest);line-height:1.5;margin-bottom:0.75rem;">"What is the role of AI in spatial design education?"</p>
        <p style="font-family:var(--f-display);font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.7;">Not about automating design — but about what changes when computational intelligence becomes a design partner. What new literacies do students need?</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
